DIS.rationale: Disney's Q2 FY26 results show solid fundamental health: revenue grew 6.5% YoY to $25.17B, operating income was stable at $4.60B, and operating cash flow surged to $6.91B. The Experiences segment remains a powerful cash engine (71.9% of segment operating income per web context), and DTC streaming achieved double-digit operating margins for the first time. Balance sheet is healthy with $115.3B equity and a manageable debt-to-equity of ~0.43-0.48. However, the trajectory is mixed: QoQ revenue declined 3.1% and EPS fell 5.2%, and YoY EPS dropped 29.8% (partly due to a high Q3 FY25 comp with $2.92 EPS). The TTM picture is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps, so I cannot confirm sustained earnings momentum. Valuation is moderately attractive: P/E of 15.1x sits near the low end of its 12.5-23.8x 12-month range, and P/B of 1.62x is near the bottom of its 1.5-2.1x range, suggesting the market is paying less for Disney's earnings power than it has over the past year. The Q2 beat-and-raise (EPS $1.57 vs $1.49 consensus, guidance raised for 12% adjusted EPS growth in FY26) and accelerated buyback ($8B target, 2.3% share count reduction YoY) provide a credible near-term rerating catalyst, as does the new CEO Josh D'Amaro's 'super-app' strategy announcement. Offsetting risks include the FCC's unprecedented early license review of ABC stations (DEI investigation, May 28 deadline), rising 10Y Treasury yields (4.47%, up 10% over 90 days) which pressure growth multiples, and elevated oil prices ($104.66/bbl) potentially weighing on international park attendance. Net-net, the combination of a solid franchise, attractive valuation vs own history, and a near-term earnings catalyst supports a mildly-to-moderately positive score, tempered by regulatory overhang and mixed sequential trends.
